name: site-expansion
description: The site grows where play goes: drilling, surveying, building and ramping past the starting square each claim the ground under them, and the whole plan still blasts on the enlarged site (#473).

steps.description: Staffed opening (#551): a driller with blasting + drill_rig licence, plus an unmanned drill_rig, are hired/purchased for free at game-open — #553's automatic drill dispatch needs both to ever land an ordered hole.
Baseline: the site is the 32x32 square the level started as.

steps.command: drill_plan add x:34 z:10 depth:6 diameter:0.089
steps.description: Was left as a bare command (role bootstrap) because whether the 3D tile picker could raycast ground still outside the site was unverified. #558 fixes exactly that -- landscape meshes now join pickScene's raycast past the claimed edge -- so this is a real click through the Drill step's point-placement tool, exercising the fix directly. diameter:0.089 added (issue #553 shared-mechanism finding, same as rock-fragmenter-breaking.json/hauling-gate.json/nav-*-visual.json): the real point-placement tool always sends the panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089 (Drill.ts), while an omitted diameter: on this console `drill_plan add` fell back to a different console-only default (0.15, mining.ts) -- computeDrillHoleDurationTicks scales drill duration by diameter, so the omission kept the drill_rig busy (fuelCostPerTick) for extra ticks command mode never should have spent, a $30 divergence at the save/load checkpoints below. Confirmed exact: adding the real default reproduces interaction mode's own $456,518 figure precisely.

expect.note: #553: site expansion (claimForAction, siteExpansion.ts) happens at order time regardless of drilling -- worldSizeX grows immediately, but the hole itself is only ordered (a PlannedHole), not yet drilled, so holeCount stays 0 until a driller/drill_rig actually lands it (see the wait step below).

steps.command: drill_plan add x:-4 z:10 depth:6 diameter:0.089
steps.description: Was left as a bare command (role bootstrap) for the same reason as the step above -- converted now that #558 lets the picker raycast past the (still-expanding) site edge.
#553: drain the ordered plan — the staffed driller/drill_rig lands both far-flung holes well inside this pad (sandbox-measured landing at tick 117).

expect.note: Both holes have landed — none lost, none left ordered forever.

steps.description: The site is wider than the level it started as.
Claimed ground is generated, not a hole: this reads as rock, not air.
Was left as a bare command (role bootstrap) for the same raycast-past-the-edge reason as the drill steps above; converted now that #558 lets the picker raycast the landscape past the site.

#555: ramp excavation is queued work, not an instant carve -- an idle driving.excavator-qualified employee from the staffed roster auto-dispatches to the rock_digger and drives it to each segment (#549's cost-based auto-claim, same mechanism drill_hole/charge_hole use; no explicit `vehicle driver` assignment needed for this, unlike building-ramp-visual's player-driven click-through). Draining it here -- before the building/charge/blast/save steps below also consume ticks -- keeps every downstream cash checkpoint (the save/load round-trip) settled against a finished ramp instead of racing this still-ticking background dig (#590/#596 convention).

expect.note: The ramp's 8 segments have all landed -- fuel/wage costs from the auto-dispatched dig are fully accrued before anything downstream reads cash.

steps.description: Was left as a bare command (role bootstrap) for the same raycast-past-the-edge reason as the steps above; converted now that #558 lets the picker raycast the landscape past the site.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

steps.command: zone clear x1:-19 y1:-5 x2:49 y2:25
steps.description: #557: evacuate the crew before firing. computeDangerZone(state.drillHoles, BLAST_DANGER_MARGIN_M) for these two holes (34,10) and (-4,10) pads out to (-19,-5)-(49,25), matching the literal box declared here -- the same rectangle Fire.ts's Sound the Horn button computes and sends. All 5 staffed employees are standing inside it (two parked exactly on the holes they just drilled, the rest working nearby). Without this, Damage.ts's processProjections (attenuated out to the full 15m BLAST_DANGER_MARGIN_M, #557) kills the entire crew the instant the blast fires -- direct-traced: deathCount 0 -> 5, and with nobody left alive, the management_office order below never finishes (no driller left to build it), stalling `wait_until buildingCount equals:1` for the rest of the file. clearZone no longer teleports: this only orders a walkout, so the wait_until step right after is what proves it actually finished.

#557: drain the real walkout Sound the Horn just ordered before firing -- NOT a wait_until on dangerZoneClear, deliberately: this box (-19,-5)-(49,25) is nearly the whole not-yet-expanded world (worldSizeX 64 from minX -16 at this point in the file, before the post-blast drill_plan add that grows it to 160), so findSafeEvacuationCell (Evacuation.ts) genuinely has no reachable cell outside it for whoever starts deep inside -- direct-traced: employees #1/#2/#3 (and the drill_rig, vehicle #1) are reported stranded, standing exactly where they were; only #4/#5, already nearer the box edge, reach a real safe cell within this pad. dangerZoneClear can never read true here -- a wait_until on it would time out by construction, not by a bug -- so this stays a fixed pad, same class as this file's own earlier `tick 120` step. Split into 3x20-tick chunks with an `event choose 0` between each (rather than one bare `tick 60`) because a bare command-mode `tick N` stops dead the instant a spontaneous event fires mid-block and never resumes on its own (command-runner.ts's own runWaitUntil doc comment) -- unlike a wait_until step, a plain command has nothing to auto-resolve it.
#557: resolves a spontaneous event if one fired during the chunk above -- see that step's own note.
A blast spanning both the original site and ground claimed during play.

#558 fence 3: a single-cell footprint with no connecting path of its own, well past the site's current frontier (chunk (2,0) is the nearest owned ground; chunk (8,0) is the target -- five intermediate chunks apart). Where the earlier drill/ramp/building steps in this file each landed on ground directly adjacent to the site (fence 1's raycast fix was the only thing standing between them and a real click), this one requires claimArea to bridge the gap itself (fence 3), well under MAX_CLAIM_BRIDGE_CHUNKS. Run immediately after the blast step (before save/load/terrain_info/state) so the blast report modal that step 'blast' just dismissed hasn't had a chance to reopen (#558 round 3) and cover this step's toolbar button. The Blast panel is already open from step 'blast' (togglePanel closes on a redundant toggle click, round 4), so this step's clicks start straight at add-hole-tool instead of re-clicking the toolbar toggle.

expect.note: #553: orderedHoleCount, not holeCount -- this hole is never drilled in this file (no wait follows), it only needs to be ordered for the site-expansion claim and the save/load round-trip below to happen; claimForAction (siteExpansion.ts) expands the site at order time regardless of drilling.

steps.description: Run the office ordered above out to a standing building before the save (#556). Placed here rather than at the order so the blast beats between the two keep the tick trajectory the file measured them at.

Left unmarked: save/load UI is out of scope for this batch -- see save-load-visual.json (Batch 6) for the real control. Runs after the far-bridging claim above, so the saved state (and the load below) includes the bridged ground at chunk (8,0), not just the original blast. #554-followup (issue #586 CI): dropped the exact `cash: 453554` -- a real CI run read 453466 ($88 off), the same real-time-accrual drift class already diagnosed and fixed for level1-playthrough-revolt.json's own cash checkpoints (see that file's notes): this step follows the `wait_until field:orderedChargeCount` charge-drain wait above, whose real per-hole charging (#554) accrues a different number of real ticks (and therefore payroll/upkeep) in interaction mode's own wall-clock pacing than in command mode's fixed tick-command trajectory -- #555's own ramp order/dig above adds a second, independent source of the same real-time-accrual drift. `changedBy: {cash: 0}` replaces it -- a real, load-bearing check that `save` itself doesn't spend or credit cash, provable in both modes regardless of which absolute value cash happens to be at this point.

Left unmarked: save/load UI is out of scope for this batch -- see save-load-visual.json (Batch 6) for the real control. The point of this round-trip: the expanded site bounds -- now including the far-bridged claim at chunk (8,0), not just the original blast -- must survive a save/load, not only a live session. #554-followup (issue #586 CI): dropped the exact `cash: 453554` here too, same real-time-accrual drift class as the save step's own note above. `changedBy: {cash: 0}` is the stronger, mode-invariant replacement for this step's actual purpose: nothing happens between `save` and `load` here, so if `load` genuinely restores the exact snapshot `save` just wrote, cash must come back unchanged from whatever it already was -- a real proof of round-trip fidelity that doesn't depend on pinning cash's own absolute value, which the two modes don't agree on to begin with.
Captures the fully-grown site, including the far-bridged claim, as persisted through the save/load round-trip above.
